resources.string: Nika is a screen reader built on Backtalk and Google TalkBack

What's new:
• v18: translator can say a word, play a sound or stay silent before translating; permission item for alarms in the clock settings; collapsible section More; gap between radial menu items; Side gestures (renamed).
• Translator: the model on the phone or an online service with your own key; actions for gestures and keys.
• Progress indicators: voice, sound, both or off; speaking in percent. The Verbosity screen is grouped into collapsible sections.
• Built-in talking clock with quiet hours (works with the screen off), countdown timer and stopwatch. Settings: «Clock, timer and stopwatch». The actions can be assigned to gestures and keys.
• New switch for the speech volume with a finger on the screen.
• Two separate gesture screens, each with its own switch: «iPhone-style gestures» (from the bottom and top edges, separate actions for the left and right half) and «Side gestures» (from the left and right edges, separate actions for the upper and lower half). Each has its own sounds, navigation button announcements and edge band width.
• Taps near the edges still work.
• Volume keys work even when the key actions switch is off.
Channel of the developer: news, questions, ideas
Actions for volume keys, number keys, arrows and other keys
Turn all the key actions below on or off Volume keys do not depend on this switch.
When off, only the combinations with Alt and other modifiers work
Leave keys alone in text fields
Volume keys still work. In a text field arrows move the cursor and digits are typed
Pause between presses (double and triple press)
Press the key you want to assign. Back cancels.
